Keywords: theft, fraud
People mentioned: Nicholas Brown
Profile:
Nicholas Brown was one of seven individuals arrested in connection with an alleged burglary ring which stole approximately USD 21m in valuables, as announced on July 24, 2019, by an officer with the Major Offenders Division of the Houston Police Department, Texas. Brown was charged with theft and burglary. 
According to officials, the valuables stolen from a residence in February 2019 included artwork, computers, guns and jewellery. Police said that the ring was connected to other thefts from high-end properties.

Profile:
Nicholas Brown of East Calder was one of six men who appeared before the High Court in Edinburgh on April 12, 2010, for sentencing in connection with the seizure of over GBP 200,000 worth of Class A drugs. All six pleaded guilty to being concerned in the supply of heroin and cocaine between February and May 2009 and Brown was sentenced to two years and six months in prison.

FSA NOTES:

Date: 7 December 2007

TAKE NOTICE: The Financial Services Authority of 25 The North Colonnade, Canary Wharf, London E14 5HS ("the FSA") gives you final notice about a decision to make a prohibition order against you:

1. THE ACTION

1.1 The FSA gave you a Decision Notice on 18 October 2006 which notified you that pursuant to section 56 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 ("the Act"), the FSA had decided to make an order prohibiting you from performing any function in relation to any regulated activity carried on by an authorised or exempt person or exempt professional firm ("the Prohibition Order").

1.2 You did not refer the matter to the Financial Services and Markets Tribunal.

Accordingly, and for the reasons set out below, the FSA hereby makes the Prohibition Order against you, effective from the date of this Final Notice.

2. REASONS FOR THE ACTION

2.1 The FSA's action is based on the findings made against you by the High Court in the case of Sphere Drake Insurance Limited and Another v Euro International Underwriting Limited and Others [2003] EWHC 1636 (Comm) in which you were a defendant as a result of your conduct as a broker placing gross loss making business in the reinsurance market in the 1990s. As more fully set out in the Summary of Facts and Conclusions annexed below, the High Court found that Sphere Drake received claims in excess of $250 million as a result of the gross loss making business passed to it and that a claim against you for dishonestly assisting in a breach of fiduciary duty succeeded (you were described as "the driving force in the dishonest enterprise"). 

The judge also found that you gave untruthful evidence during the trial.

resolution.comment: Citizenship and residence inconsistent with the subject; discounted.

sections.label: Profile Notes
data:
Keywords: narcotics, fraud
People mentioned: Nicholas Brown, David Aurele Wait
Profile:
Nicholas Brown, a resident of Pottsville, Pennsylvania, was one of a total of 13 individuals who were arrested on suspicion of involvement in a prescription drug fraud ring, as reported on March 5, 2015.
According to the indictment, David Aurele Wait, a medical doctor based in New Cumberland, Pennsylvania, wrote hundreds of bogus prescriptions for the co-defendants in the case. Wait allegedly prescribed oxycodone, a powerful synthetic opiate, without even meeting or examining the purported recipients of the prescriptions. Between January 2013 and June 2014, Wait allegedly wrote prescriptions for 102,000 oxycodone pills. The bogus prescriptions were filled at pharmacies in Cumberland, Dauphin, Lebanon, Perry, York and Allegheny counties.
Brown was charged with a single count of obtaining a controlled substance by fraud.
